summary: Our project is an interactive digital storytelling experience designed for school-age space enthusiasts to explore NASA’s historic discarded hardware on the Moon and Mars. Rather than viewing these relics as mere space debris, we frame them as humanity’s silent cosmic time capsules from the final emotional message of the Opportunity rover to the laser-reflecting mirrors on the lunar surface. We address the challenge of making aerospace history engaging and educational for young minds by blending interactive design with compelling narratives, bridging the gap between past robotic missions and future space exploration.
details: Abandoned but Not Forgotten tells the story of NASA’s retired Moon and Mars machines for school-age space enthusiasts, with each machine speaking for itself in the first person. We built the Silent Explorer Method, a four-step process (find, verify, scale down, give it a voice) that turns raw NASA data into short stories, with one rule: every number has a NASA source. Our flagship story follows the Mars rover Opportunity, which was planned for 90 days but worked for 5,111 Mars days and drove 45.16 km before a global dust storm silenced it in 2018. We also outlined stories for Sojourner, Spirit, InSight, Ingenuity and the Apollo hardware on the Moon. We used NASA/JPL mission pages, the Planetary Data System, the NASA Image and Video Library and the Apollo archives. An AI assistant (Claude, by Anthropic) helped draft the text and presentation, and all facts are based on these NASA sources. Next, we will test the stories with students in Adana and publish them in Turkish and English, open to everyone.
